subject: Throughput exception request — canary embedder (temporary)
messages:
From: Emma Holden <emma@orbital.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-20T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary throughput concession for Orbital embedder canary

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re kicking off a week-long canary with our new embedder (v0.9-beta) starting Monday and we’re seeing burst patterns that exceed the default throughput windows in the Hosted plan. Can you advise whether Redwood can provide a short-term throughput/latency concession for the canary — specifically, a temporary 3-day exception to the per-tenant concurrency cap and a relaxed 95th percentile latency SLO (from 250ms to 500ms) for the canary traffic only?

High level:
- We’ll route ~4k users (internal + pilot customers) through the canary.
- Expected peak sustained qps: ~180 rps for 30–90 minute bursts.
- We will add client-side rate limiting if you ask; our goal is to run a realistic stress window to validate model quality under load.

Do you need any logs or a traffic plan — happy to share a short runbook and the canary schedule. If possible we’d like a decision by COB Friday so we can align onboarding.

Thanks,
Emma Holden
Director, Product
Orbital Analytics

Karthik / team — I ran the sim against our canary pool with the numbers Emma sent. Short notes:
- Baseline pool (2x p4d-8) handles ~60 rps steady with 95th ≈ 220ms.
- To sustain 180 rps spikes we need either: (A) +2 additional GPUs (preferred) or (B) traffic shaping + degraded model variant (quantized) to keep CPU bounded.
- Auto-fallback: if token latency > 500ms for > 3m or error rate > 1.5% we need to initiate model fallback to v0.8 (quantized) and divert traffic to dedicated pool.

Operational ask of Orbital: provide a 10-minute sample of peak traffic (cURL + headers) and the CIDR ranges all requests will originate from. I attached a short canary-run log extract to show simulated CPU/mem during a 90m sustained burst.

—Dev

Thanks all — drafted language below for a 72-hour, scoped exception. Please review and flag anything missing before I convert to a PDF addendum.

Draft addendum summary:
- Scope: Exception applies only to traffic from CIDRs 52.11.0.0/16 and 34.200.0.0/16 identified in Appendix A and only to requests routed to model family "embedder-v0.9-beta".
- Duration: 72 hours starting 2026-08-31T09:00:00-07:00 (UTC-7).
- SLO adjustments: 95th percentile token latency threshold increased from 250ms to 500ms for the canary cohort only.
- Capacity: Redwood will provision +2 GPUs in the canary pool for the window.
- Rollback triggers: sustained >1.5% 5xx or 95th latency >600ms for >5 minutes will trigger automatic rollback to embedder-v0.8 (quantized) and re-route to the standard pool.
- Monitoring & reporting: Redwood will provide hourly telemetry to Orbital; a final post-mortem within 72 hours of completion.

Questions for Legal/Sales: do we need a credit/waiver clause for any SLA breaches during the canary? If so, suggested cap = 10% credit on billed inference usage for the canary window.

Mina
